Target: Apple (AAPL). Apple develops and sells personal computing devices including iPhone, Mac and iPad, with operating systems and digital services.

Focal announcement: Apple reports first quarter results.

Decision cutoff: 2026-01-29T23:59:59-05:00. Only information available before this cutoff is admissible.

Source: Apple reports first quarter results. Published: 2026-01-29. URL: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/01/apple-reports-first-quarter-results.

Condensed source facts; other details are omitted: CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced financial results for its fiscal 2026 first quarter ended December 27, 2025. “Today, Apple is proud to report a remarkable, record-breaking quarter, with revenue of $143.8 billion, up 16 percent from a year ago and well above our expectations,” said Tim Cook, Apple’s CEO. “iPhone had its best-ever quarter driven by unprecedented demand, with all-time records across every geographic segment, and Services also achieved an all-time revenue record, up 14 percent from a year ago. “During the December quarter, our record business performance and strong margins led to EPS growth of 19 percent, setting a new all-time EPS record,” said Kevan Parekh, Apple’s CFO. “These exceptionally strong results generated nearly $54 billion in operating cash flow, allowing us to return almost $32 billion to shareholders.”

The exact historical text version is unverified. This is an incomplete source-based reconstruction.

Expectations: No point-in-time analyst consensus or market-implied expectation is available.

No company-wide comparable financial baselines or incremental magnitude inputs were supplied. Do not infer that a large headline amount is material to the target.

The stock showed a modest past rise over the latest completed session, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock showed a substantial past rise over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock showed a substantial past decline over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The stock's recent daily variability was moderate. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

The broad market (SPY) showed a modest past decline over the latest completed session, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a modest past rise over the recent trading week, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY) showed a modest past rise over the recent trading month, judged against its recent ordinary variability.

The broad market (SPY)'s recent daily variability was relatively subdued. Variability describes the size of ordinary fluctuations, not their future direction.

Over the recent trading week, the stock showed substantial outperformance relative to the broad market.

Over the recent trading month, the stock showed substantial underperformance relative to the broad market.

These are coarse descriptions computed from observed historical inputs. Strong past movement or relative strength is not evidence that the next return must continue or reverse.

The previously fitted market-only reference model favored an upward return beyond the neutral band. Its leading outcome was only slightly favored. It still assigned meaningful possibility to a return inside the narrow neutral band and a downward return beyond the neutral band. This is a training-only model forecast, not an observed outcome or independent news evidence.

The neutral return band's half-width is narrower than the code-computed ordinary five-session variability scale. An irrelevant article does not eliminate ordinary price movement; this is not a calculated class probability.

Forecast target: entry is the first regular-session open after the cutoff; exit is the fifth session close, counting entry as session one. Raw return above +1% is up; within inclusive -1% to +1% is flat; below -1% is down. The initial pre-entry reaction is outside this target.

Do not invent analyst consensus, incremental target sales, new corporate cash payments, or an already-priced news reaction.
